articleTitle: The International Comparison of Learners’ Knowledge and Awareness in Japanese Technology Education: A Comparative study of middle and high school students against Japan, Indonesia, China, and the United States of America
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: The study aims to evaluate current Japanese information technology education against Japan, Indonesia, China, and the United States of America and develop Japanese technology education via an international comparative survey on learners’ technology education knowledge and awareness. The results demonstrate differences in Japan’s 1) desire to utilize information and communication technologies (ICT) recreationally as opposed to professionally; 2) willingness to participate in industrial technology education (ITE) or information technology education; and 3) technology familiarity is comparatively lower than in other countries examined. Based on these results, Japanese technology education needs future development in terms of both curriculum and teaching materials.

articleTitle: The Audiobook Project Based Learning: An Approach Aimed at Improving Students’ English Reading Fluency
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: Since one of the objectives of the English in Focus (EIF) class was to help students improve their reading fluency, the research aimed to investigate the effects of an audiobook project on students’ reading fluency in the EIF class based on students’ perception. The participants were students from two EIF classes, for a total of eighty-three students. The investigation was conducted using a qualitative approach, and the data were gathered using a questionnaire. The questionnaire was divided into two parts: the first consisted of fifteen statements accompanied by a Likert scale, and the second contained two open-ended questions designed to collect more detailed information. Within 7 meetings, the audiobook implementation project was successfully finished. After finishing the audiobook project, the students’ reading fluency and experience were significantly enhanced, as demonstrated by the results of the research. During the course of working on the audiobook project, students were able to demonstrate correct intonation and articulation when reading English text, learned new words, and improved their ability to work together on the project by discussing it with the other members of their group. In conclusion, based on students’ perception, the research findings indicate that implementing an audiobook project to improve reading fluency is viable.

articleTitle: The Design of VBee Diary Writing Application
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: The development of critical thinking, creativity, and communication abilities is facilitated by the acquisition of writing skills, which are significant for students. Nevertheless, a considerable number of students presently encounter difficulties in locating the impetus and enthusiasm required for engagement in writing endeavors. The focus of the present paper is application design. The VBee application is a web-based application that facilitates the expression of user creativity and fosters a deeper appreciation for the art of writing. The application boasts a highly intuitive interface that effortlessly enables users to document their thoughts and experiences. It offers a plethora of features that not only facilitate writing but also foster self-expression, including customizable emoticons and the option to provide feedback. By designing the application, it could help support vocational school students in improving the quality of skill-focused education, particularly their English creative writing skill in enjoyment. Besides, the teachers are assisted to guide their students with technologically advanced and entertaining learning tools.

articleTitle: Functional Credit Score Application Using Rule-Based System for Vocational School Teachers
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: The development of technology and information can be one aspect of improving the quality of education. One of the efforts that can be made is to digitally develop innovative credit score calculations for teachers. The credit score itself is the right for a teacher who has carried out professional activities following the abilities and fields that are mastered. The observations’ results on calculating credit scores at SMKN 2 Singosari are still done manually. These problems can be overcome by developing information-based systems for calculating teacher credit scores at SMKN 2 Singosari with the SDLC system development method or system Development Life Cycle model Waterfall. The results of the research show that the credit score calculation application is a website developed to obtain an average percentage of the results of functionality testing of all access rights of 96.18% and the results of usability testing of all access rights of 96.72% with the results of tests conducted by information system experts obtaining a validity percentage of 99.26% for functionality testing and a validity percentage of 93.61% for usability testing which is declared fit for use in the SMK Negeri 2 Singosari environment.

articleTitle: Investigating VIAT-Map from the view point of Ease of Use, Perceived of Usefulness, and Acceptance of IT by using Technology Acceptance Model (TAM)
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: The use of technology in the classroom is becoming a common situation. With the development of science in the field of learning technology, support for the learning process is getting better and wider. However, in Indonesia, the use of learning technology is only limited to E-learning, videos and LMS which lack interaction in the learning process and are closer to the assessment process only. Viat-map is a learning application that focuses on increasing students’ understanding of literacy materials. Using Toulmin’s Argumentation pattern and combined with constructivism theory, Viat-map applications produce positive results during the experimental process. In addition, the application also supports the process of feedback. Lecturers will be given an overlapping analysis that shows the location of students’ thinking errors. By doing all stages of learning using Viat-map, it is expected to be able to provide a new positive perspective on class activities. This study involved twenty-seven participants consisting of twenty-six students and one teacher. The learning process uses the viat-map application for two weeks. After that, they were given the Questionaire of Technology Acceptance Model and got positive results on the acceptance of the use of learning technology in the classroom.

articleTitle: Challenges in the Post-Pandemic Era: Examining the Influence of Self-Regulated Learning on Academic Stress Among Students in Indonesian Higher Education Institutions
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: The primary aim of this research is to examine the possible impact of self-regulated learning (SRL) on the levels of academic stress encountered by students enrolled in various university in Indonesia. Quantitative research methods are grounded in the systematic measurement of quantities or values. The data-gathering methodology employed in this study was the utilization of a survey instrument. The survey constitutes a quantitative research undertaking that utilizes a standardized set of structured questions, which are uniformly presented to all participants. The impact of SRL on the magnitude of academic stress encountered by tertiary students in Indonesia is not significant. The phenomenon can be attributed to a multitude of potential factors, including diminished student motivation, diminished support networks, and inadequate time management skills. This finding suggests that the questionnaire exhibits a degree of inconsistency, indicating the need for future researchers to develop or employ other scales that offer greater reliability, especially in the post-pandemic era.

articleTitle: The Influence of Using WhatsApp, Zoom, and Google Meet as Group-Based Online Communication Techniques on the Performance of School Administrative Staff
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: Currently, the school quality of education in Indonesia is still low. One of the reasons for the low quality of education is the weakness of school management. One of the causes of the poor quality of school management is that administrative staff could not assist the leadership in carrying out or managing the school optimally. This research aims to examine the influence of group-based online communication techniques, namely WhatsApp, Zoom, and Google Meet, on the performance of school administrative staff. This study applies a correlational descriptive research design. Seventy-four samples were taken from Batu, Probolinggo, and Sidoarjo using a cluster random sampling technique. The data analysis technique uses descriptive statistics and Pearson’s Product Moment correlation. The research results show a significant influence of group-based online communication techniques on the performance of school administration staff. There is no significant influence on the partial use of WhatsApp, Zoom, and Google Meet on the performance of school administration staff.

articleTitle: Students’ Engagement in Computational Thinking Skills Using A Game Based-Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: This study aims to investigate students’ engagement in computational thinking skills through game-based learning in science classrooms. Data was gathered through observation and interviews with 30 secondary school students. Research data were analyzed qualitatively through six stages involving preparing and organizing data, exploring data, developing descriptions, representing results, interpreting findings, and validating the accuracy of findings. The study results show that game-based learning makes students engaged in computational thinking skills. Interaction with educational games trains students to find solutions more precisely and bravely in making decisions. Game-based learning can be a solution to introduce students’ computational thinking skills in a more enjoyable way. Teachers are expected to use this research to teach students computational thinking skills through game-based learning.

articleTitle: Simulation of Data Acquisition System Using SimulIDE, Virtual Serial Port and Python
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: Data acquisition systems are commonplace in the current era of digitalization and Industry 4.0. These systems are typically used to obtain data from sensors, whether analog or digital, which is then stored for processing in subsequent stages. However, the implementation of hardware for creating data acquisition systems can be challenging due to constraints such as laboratory facilities, budget limitations, and other factors. Therefore, in this research, SimulIDE simulation software was employed to simulate electronic components and the Arduino Uno. To make this virtual Arduino appear as a physical one to the host computer, PyVirtualSerialPorts was used as a virtual serial port. The data acquisition system was created using Python programming with several key features: it can store data in CSV format, present data plots and graphs, and display the frequency spectrum of signals. The system achieved a sampling speed of 1000 data points per second, with input signals limited to a maximum of 10 Hz. This study also shows that signal distortion can occur due to excessively frequent data plotting and Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) processing. Therefore, the use of SimulIDE simulator, virtual serial port, and Python can be utilized in the learning process of a simple data acquisition system.

articleTitle: Predicting Students’ Learning Outcomes in Massive Open Online Courses
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: E-learning has now become a common learning delivery method, especially in higher education during the Covid-19 pandemic. One of the obstacles faced by instructors through this method is the difficulty of observing the behavior of learning participants directly, even though the learning is presented synchronously, moreover, learning mode is presented asynchronously. However, currently, this problem can be coped with utilizing the field of Educational Data Mining (EDM). Some features or types of data sets are processed to produce important information from a learning management system. This type of dataset is divided into three categories, namely: 1) log file features 2) Forum Activities, 3) Evaluation activities feature. Predictive Learning Analytics (PLA) is one of the commonly used techniques in the field of learning analytics and EDM, this technique provides instructors with an understanding to predict the learning success of participants and how to find problems faced by them. This research focused on activities that can describe the students’ achievement.

articleTitle: An Overview on Virtual Guest Lecture in EFL Classroom Context: A Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: Amidst the COVID-19 pandemic, virtual guest lectures have assumed paramount importance in university education, extending teaching beyond the traditional classroom setting. This study undertook a systematic review to investigate the schematic structure and linguistic features of virtual guest lectures in the context of English as a Foreign Language (EFL) classrooms. Employing Kitchenman’s systematic review methodology, we compiled a dataset from SCOPUS and SINTA databases comprising 10 published journal articles from 2019 to 2022. The analysis was grounded in the Systemic Functional Linguistics (SFL) approach. Our findings revealed that virtual guest lectures exhibit a three-phase schematic structure: introduction, content, and concluding phases. The introduction phase encompasses three distinct moves, including greeting, class checking, and orientation. In the content phase, three moves were identified: presentation, discussion, and consolidation. Finally, the concluding phase encompasses evaluation, reflection, and closure. Furthermore, in terms of linguistic realizations, we identified relational, mental, behavioral, and material processes within each move or step. These findings offer valuable insights for educational stakeholders, aiding in the evaluation and assessment of student achievements during virtual guest lectures. Moreover, they provide a foundation for potential enhancements in the design and delivery of virtual guest lectures in EFL classrooms.

articleTitle: Measuring Augmented Reality Effectiveness on ESP Students’ Reading Comprehension
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: This study aims to investigate the impact of Augmented Reality (AR) effectiveness on English Specific Purposes (ESP) students' reading comprehension ability. A quasi-experimental research design was employed. The participants were ESP students majoring Information Technology Department of State Polytechnic of Malang. Additionally, the subjects were randomly assigned to two groups, either the experimental or control group. The experimental group received an AR-based reading comprehension treatment, while the control group received a traditional teaching method without AR technology. Pre-test and post-test were administered to both groups to measure their reading comprehension skills. Quantitative data analysis was conducted using statistical techniques in Paired Samples T-test and ANOVA. The findings revealed that the experimental group, exposed to AR technology, demonstrated significantly higher improvement in reading comprehension scores compared to the control group. These results suggested that AR implementation had a positive impact on ESP students' reading comprehension abilities, providing an immersive and interactive learning experience. The implications of this research highlight the potential of integrating AR technology into ESP curriculum design to enhance reading comprehension skills and improve overall learning outcomes for ESP students.

articleTitle: Kemudi: A Mobile Application for Learning to Drive a Car in Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: Car driving activities have become one of the needs of people in Indonesia. This leads to the importance of understanding how to drive properly and correctly. This study discusses designing a driving education mobile application in Indonesia called “Kemudi”. This study aims to provide material on driving theory under traffic rules in Indonesia. Application design using the Rapid Application Development (RAD) software development method. Applications are designed using the Flutter framework, which is then evaluated using the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology 2 (UTAUT2). The evaluation results showed that users were satisfied with aspects of facilitating condition (91.56%), social influence (91.33%), price value (89.33%), effort expectancy (88.83%), hedonic motivation (87.67%), performance expectancy (86.33%), behavioral intention (81.33%), habit (78.67%). The results of this study can support people learning how to drive a car through the mobile application.

articleTitle: Lesson Practice on Design of Turbine for Ocean Current Power Generation Using Simple 3DCAD
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: The purpose of this study is to construct a teaching process that integrates the learning of “materials and processing technology” and “energy conversion technology” using “design of turbines for ocean current power generation” as the subject matter, and to verify the effectiveness of the teaching practice. Specifically, in the “Materials and Processing Technology” class, students learned the design and fabrication of turbines using 3D CAD software, as well as the polishing and finishing of turbines. In the “Energy Conversion Technology” class, students learned about the mechanism of ocean current power generation and the differences in power generation efficiency depending on turbine shape through experiments. As a result, the students were able to engage in design and fabrication activities with interest in fabrication activities using 3D CAD software and 3D printers, and they also enjoyed the classes. In addition, it was suggested that the students’ interest in ocean current power generation and the global environment increased, and their awareness of saving electricity and using renewable energy increased

articleTitle: Perception Analysis of Web-based Thesis Management System using Short-User Experience Questionnaire (UEQ-S)
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: User experience (UX) is a pivotal determinant of a product’s success in the competitive market. Acknowledging this significance, the Short User Experience Questionnaire (UEQ-S), a succinct variant of the UEQ, emerges as a fitting assessment tool. This research employs the UEQ-S questionnaire to gauge user experiences within the context of a web-based Thesis Management System called SINTESIS. With its 8-item structure, UEQ-S captures users’ perspectives across a 7-point scale, allowing for quick and comprehensive evaluations. Twenty master student participants were involved as respondents to this study. The reliability of gathered data was rigorously evaluated using Cronbach’s alpha measurement. The empirical findings from conducted experiments illuminate that the developed system elicits positive feedback, indicating a favorable reception. The outcomes underscore the utility of UEQ-S as a potent instrument for quantifying and optimizing user experiences, facilitating informed design decisions, and fostering enhanced product quality.

articleTitle: Developing the Beekita BIPA App for Enhanced Vocabulary Acquisition in BIPA Students
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: This study focuses on elevating children’s acquisition of BIPA (Indonesian Language for Foreign Speakers) vocabulary via the Beekita BIPA application. Employing the 4D model (Define, Design, Development, Dissemination), this research encompasses meticulous developmental stages. Outcomes reveal customized vocabulary learning for children at A-1 and A-2 levels, encompassing self-presentation, numerals, days, family, and daily life. The Beekita BIPA application integrates corpus analysis, “Sahabatku Indonesia A-1” textbook, and online resources to craft its vocabulary. It offers a range of features: a start page, immersive introduction through “Bee,” usage instructions, thematic choices mirroring Indonesian islands, vocabulary exposition with pronunciation, educational games, and digital stamps as rewards. Expert evaluation confirms the application’s alignment with pedagogical standards, age-appropriate design, linguistic norms, interactivity, and cognitive aptitude. Empirical trials underscore its visual appeal, motivational potency, clear audio, and aesthetic quality. In conclusion, this study navigates developmental, pedagogical, and evaluative realms, enriching children’s BIPA vocabulary acquisition. Anchored in “Enhancing Children’s BIPA Vocabulary Learning through the Beekita BIPA Application,” it opens pathways for pedagogical innovations in language education.

articleTitle: Syntagmatic Distractor Generation for Vocabulary Multiple Choice Questions
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: Learning assessments that are currently conducted online pose new problems for educators as they demand extensive resources, take time, and require a deep understanding of the materials involved. Standardized English tests that have been used for a long time often use a multiple-choice format for convenience in scoring. The problem with creating multiple-choice questions for vocabulary tests is how to generate distractors that are plausible while not being acceptable as answers. This research focused on generating distractors for vocabulary questions that were syntagmatically related to the reading passage. To date, there has not yet been any research that focuses on the syntagmatic aspect of generating English vocabulary distractors for multiple-choice questions. This research generated distractor candidates from the LinguaTools word collocation dictionary that were filtered according to part of speech and syntactic relation, then ranked by the significance of co-occurring relevance to the context. We generated distractors for vocabulary questions which were then evaluated by educators in high schools and colleges who were experts in setting English tests. The results of the proposed method indicated that 80.83% of generated distractors qualified as vocabulary items for multiple-choice questions.

articleTitle: Effect of Camera Simulator Application for Basic Photography Subjects at Vocational School: One-Group Pre-test and Post-test Design
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: This study examines the impact of using the camera simulator application in basic photography subjects for students cognitive skills majoring in broadcasting and film in vocational high schools in Indonesia. Camera simulators have the advantage of providing opportunities for students to practice more freely and independently. In this study, the CamSim Pro application was employed as the camera simulator and was installed on desktop systems. Eighty eligible students from Public Vocational High School (PVHS) 10 Bandung participated in using the camera simulator as an intervention technology in two topics in basic photography subjects: aperture priority mode and shutter priority. This study adopts a quasi-experimental research method with a one-group pre-test and post-test design, examining the impact of camera simulator intervention. This research uses five stages, (1) designing the pre-test and its evaluation, (2) selecting the group/population to be tested, (3) preparing and providing a camera simulator intervention, (4) designing the post-test and evaluating it, and (5) conducting data analysis referring to the results of the pre-test and the post-test. The data normality test uses the Kolgomorov-Smirnov method and the Shapiro-Wilk method. Data analysis to measure the impact of technological interventions uses the Wilcoxon Signed Ranks method and the significance of the technological interventions using the Z statistic and asymptotic significance. Analysis of the collected data unveiled a compelling narrative. The Z statistic exhibited a notable value of −4.897, paired with an asymptotic significance value of < 0.001. These findings support the hypothesis that integrating a camera simulator to facilitate learning significantly enhances students’ cognitive skills in fundamental photography subjects.

articleTitle: Proposal for Effective Use of ICT to Support Collaboration between Classroom and Home Study
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: While ICT-based learning environments have been established in recent years through the GIGA school concept, its use at home is still in its growth stage. This paper constructs an instructional process that combines a junior high school home economics technology class and home study, and examines its effectiveness through classroom practice. After the class practice, 40 second-year junior high school students were asked to self-evaluate their efforts on a worksheet, and their responses were analyzed. The analysis results showed that students were actively engaged in inquiry activities at home by devising support for the four hours of class and home study, and that through the linkage of ICT-based class and home study, a place for inquiry-based learning was formed through individual and collaborative learning. This is believed to have led to an awareness of the viewpoints and ideas of technology that aim to realize a sustainable society and to properly evaluate and optimize technology from economic, environmental, and other perspectives.

Author Keywords: junior high school technology and home economics (technology field)

articleTitle: Ethics of Using Digital Technology with E-Training among Computer Science Students Internship Program for a Resilient Future
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: The purpose of this study was to find out to what extent computer science internship program students instilled ethics in using digital technology with e-training from their perspectives, to analyze the average estimate of students in practicing ethical use of digital technology, and to see the goals of students teaching the ethics of using digital technology using e-training. The research method used is a quantitative dominant mixed method with the number of respondents being 150 computer science students participating in the teacher apprenticeship program at Brawijaya University. The data analysis software used in the study was IBM SPSS Statistics 22. The results of the study included (a) overall degree of computer science internship program for ethical practice of using digital technology with e-training was students’ ethical practices towards others and practice students ethical towards themselves; (b) average score of students in computer science internship programs and ethical practices in the use of digital technology with high e-training is (M = 3.93) understanding free software; and (c) the highest goal of computer science internship program students who practice the ethics of using digital technology with e-training for a sustainable future is 30% to have morality and ethics.

articleTitle: Strengthening Educators’ Skills: Lessons from the Pandemic Era
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: COVID-19 has had various effects on education. It has alerted authorities to the need for online and distance education that is more feasible. Further, it has (re)introduced several educational tools and platforms. What occurs now that the world has entered the endemic stage? This paper addresses the question of how educators at the National Defense University of Malaysia (NDUM) can prepare for analogous situations to COVID-19. Consequently, two research queries are formulated. First, what lessons could be learned about teaching during the pandemic, and second, how should one best prepare for the uncertain future of teaching? This paper’s methodology included a content analysis of previously published papers with similar research interests and the author’s experience when she participated in an emergency remote teaching practice for the first time. Preliminary findings reveal the importance of preparing students, educators, and institutions for the unknown; this paper concentrates on physical or digital presences of educators, which is essential for ensuring effective teaching and learning. Given these, hybrid/hyflex teaching necessitates an equal presence of educators in both physical and online instruction. This demonstrates the significance of encouraging educators to enhance their physical and online presences so that students can participate in meaningfully engaging learning.

articleTitle: Implementation of E-Mudharabah Application as A Learning Media for Islamic Economics Accounting Using Formative Assessments Method
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: The primary objective of this research is to simplify the understanding of the Mudharabah concept and facilitate the development of the scheme by integrating diverse financing methods such as ROI, IRR, and NPV. Additionally, this initiative aims to furnish students with an in-depth comprehension of the various roles involved in this scheme, including the investor (Shahib Al-Maal), consultant, and recipient of funds (Mudharib). To attain these objectives, the "change role" feature is implemented within the E-Mudharabah application, enabling users to switch roles and comprehend the Mudharabah process from different perspectives. The application content is made in such a way as to facilitate a comprehensive understanding. Furthermore, a formative assessment approach was utilized for evaluation purposes. This method was employed to determine the effectiveness of the learning medium in aiding both students and educators in comprehending the complexities of the Mudharabah financing process, through the utilization of a range of diverse financing analysis methods. The results obtained from the E-Mudharabah application using the formative assessment approach indicate that 86% of respondents reported the effectiveness of the learning medium. It means the application's success in delivering clear content, as well as providing an interactive and meaningful learning experience for its users.

articleTitle: Exploring Synchronous and Asynchronous Technological Applications and Challenges in Online English Language Classrooms in Indonesia and Thailand
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: This research explores synchronous and asynchronous technological applications used and challenges experienced by teachers and students Indonesia and Thailand, especially in online English language classrooms. This research employs a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) approach, selecting 47 research papers published between 2020-2022 from Google Scholar and Scopus database. The results show that, in Indonesia, teachers and students used applications like Google Meet, Zoom, Microsoft Team, Cisco WebEx, Discord, GoToMeeting, FreeConference, YouTube Live Streaming, and Skype for synchronous online leaning and WhatsApp, Moodle, YouTube, Powtoon, Screen O’Matic, Instagram, Kahoot, Quizzes, Google Form, BeeSmart, Schoology, Autodesk SketchBook, TED-Ed, FastStone Capture, Ruang Guru Edmodo, Telegram, Spada. And OmegaT for asynchronous online learning. Meanwhile, in Thailand, they utilized Google Meet, Zoom, Microsoft Team, and Facebook Live for synchronous online learning and Google Doc, Google Form, Socrative, Facebook, Instagram, Line, Twitter, YouTube, Kahoot, Quizzes, Quizlet, Quizlet for asynchronous online learning. They also faced several challenges such as unstable internet connection, lack of technological literacy, incompatible gadgets, unconducive learning environment, limited participation, work overload, academic misconduct, and poor time management. The results can be used by relevant stakeholders to help incorporate synchronous and asynchronous online learning and prepare for future learning.

articleTitle: Bibliometric Historiography of Important Document on Electronic Leadership Research
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: This research was conducted using bibliometric historiography with a visualization approach to comprehensively understand the evolution of the field of e-Leadership. The data source of this research is a database obtained from the Web of Science, a total of 185 documents from 1997 to 2022. The software used to analyze the data is HistCite. Descriptive statistical analysis and bibliometric historiography are used to determine development trends in the field of e-Leadership. This study presents a significant paper, which is categorized as a paper that has a major influence on the development of the field of e-Leadership, based on the Local Citation Score. Practical and theoretical implications are discussed, and future research possibilities have also been suggested.

articleTitle: Study Case on Implementation Elevator 2 Floor System on PLC OMRON CP1E N30
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: The swift progression of industrial technology underscores the need for adept professionals capable of skillfully implementing and managing intricate systems. Vocational education assumes a pivotal role in cultivating competent intermediaries proficient in translating theoretical knowledge into practical applications. At the core of industrial automation lies the Programmable Logic Controller (PLC), a specialized digital computer that interfaces with sensors, switches, and actuators to execute real-time control programs, thus facilitating meticulous industrial processes. This study concentrates on the practical deployment of a two-floor elevator system utilizing the OMRON CP1E N30 PLC. Elevators, integral to contemporary structures, mandate precision for secure vertical conveyance. Leveraging input signals from elevator buttons, sensors, and switches, the PLC orchestrates efficient motor control and dependable door operations. This hands-on application underscores the PLC’s significance within real-time control contexts. Nonetheless, Vocational Higher Education graduates frequently grapple with the challenge of transitioning to industry settings due to limited practical exposure. This partnership harmonizes with the center’s objective of enriching vocational education by integrating sophisticated technologies like PLCs, equipping the workforce with the acumen to bridge the gap between theoretical foundations and the pragmatic demands of industry.

articleTitle: Modeling User Profile in Gamification Based e-Learning Using k-Means Clustering
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: The current development of e-Learning is still in the form of simple e-Learning as a place to share materials and do the exercises given by lecturers. This should be a problem since such e-Learning activities are not different from conventional learning and do not facilitate a personalized learning process. Personalized learning is important to address students’ different comprehension abilities in the learning process. Personalization can be done by characterizing student profiles. Therefore, we need a system to determine profiles by modeling user profiles in e-Learning. In this study, personalization was done by recognizing the users’ characteristics obtained from internal factors including personality, achievement emotion, and student activity logs when engaging in the e-Learning process. Student activity logs were automatically recorded by the system. To find out the profile of existing user, grouping was done using the unsupervised machine learning method, namely k-Means Clustering. Two k-clusters were employed to determine the user profiles. Two grouped profiles indicated differences in characteristics of the user profile group. The results of the cluster evaluation show the value of Silhouette Score of 0.43 and Connectivity Score of 8.85.

articleTitle: Investigation and Analysis of Teaching Contents on Interfaces in Japanese Secondary Education
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: In modern times, citizens utilize various services through the Internet and cloud computing to enhance their convenience in daily life. Communication, business, and shopping are conducted online, reducing constraints of time and space. The diverse interfaces supporting this information technology have been addressed differently in the fields of technology education and home economics in middle schools and in the field of information science in high schools. The curriculum guidelines have revealed that hardware interfaces are covered in the technology education field, while software interfaces are covered in the information science field. The purpose of this study is to examine how these interfaces have been treated in these educational settings and to consider future educational content regarding interfaces.

Author Keywords: junior high school technology and home economics (technology field)

articleTitle: AI Perspectives in Education: A BERT-based Exploration of Informatics Students’ Attitudes to ChatGPT
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: This study examined informatics students’ perspectives on ChatGPT through sentiment analysis, utilizing advanced BERT neural networks within Python to understand their sentiments comprehensively. By harnessing BERT’s intricate contextual embeddings and attention mechanisms, we effectively evaluated the subtleties of students’ attitudes. Our methodology encompassed categorizing student ChatGPT reviews using a 5-star rating scale, capturing diverse sentiments and enabling scrutiny of their distribution and trends. Positive sentiments were predominant, as students lauded ChatGPT’s potential as a valuable academic tool. Its capacity to assist in research, assignments, and information retrieval garnered significant praise. However, neutral and negative sentiments pinpointed areas for improvement. Neutral sentiments indicated potential optimization, while negative sentiments flagged inaccuracies and response time concerns. Ultimately, this amalgamation of sentiment analysis and BERT insights provided a lucid view of informatics students’ interactions with ChatGPT. In conclusion, the fusion of sentiment analysis and BERT insights has spotlighted ChatGPT’s immense potential as an academic companion. This study underscores its value as an effective support tool, emphasizing the commitment to continuous enhancement. By diligently refining ChatGPT, we can enhance its performance, tailor it more precisely to students’ diverse needs, and seamlessly empower them to integrate AI-driven language models into their educational journeys.

articleTitle: An Investigation and Analysis Of Digital Human Resources Demanded by Society in Technical Education
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: In recent years, the fourth industrial revolution has been progressing with ICT, IoT, and AI used for processing big data. In the manufacturing industry, not only product design using 3D CAD but also CAE via 3D data and production with prototyping and testing via simulation technology is becoming more common. In technical education, there is a need for effective education that utilizes these digital technologies to teach the digital technologies that society demands. Therefore, the purpose of this research was to obtain basic knowledge by investigating digital technology among engineers and managers involved in the manufacturing industry and examining the content of education of the future. Specifically, we have investigated the purpose and problem in the introduction and situation of digital technology, human resources development to utilize digital technology, and qualities and skills to find manufacturing human resources. As a result, it was found that there is a tendency to seek human resources who have knowledge and skills in 3D CAD, CAM, and CNC machines, which are widely used in the process of manufacturing, as there is a desire to introduce advanced technologies such as AI and VR with a lack of the know-how to handle them. These findings have led to proposals for digital technology to be acquired and content to be taught in technical education.

articleTitle: IoT Application in Indonesian Vocational Schools as Learning Media and Learning Support Infrastructure: A Systematic Review
publicationTitle: 2023 9th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: With its capabilities, the Internet of Things (IoT) in the education sector can be implemented to increase the efficiency and effectiveness of learning. IoT can be used as learning media and learning support infrastructure in the learning process in vocational education. This study aims to identify and study various IoT-based innovations implemented as learning media and learning support infrastructure in vocational education in Indonesia. A systematic review searches various published scientific papers with defined search criteria. The search results are studied based on publication trends, the type of IoT technology applied, the level of technology readiness, and an evaluation of the implementation of IoT. Through a search process using Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-analyses (PRISMA) method, 16 relevant articles were found. The analysis results show that most of the publications were published in the last two years (38%) in journals and conferences. Seventy-five percent of the articles were in English, and 94% of the publications came from provinces in the Java Island. The Technology Readiness Level (TRL) of implementing IoT is 81% at level 4-5. This research shows that there are still wide-open opportunities for implementing IoT as learning media and learning support infrastructure for vocational education in Indonesia.
